summary.name: Service Levels and Error Budgets
summary.one_liner: A 2016 SREcon16 conference talk by Google SREs Chris Jones and Niall Murphy on setting service level objectives and using error budgets instead of 100% reliability targets.
use_cases: Deciding on a realistic reliability target for a service
Understanding how SLOs differ from SLAs and SLIs
Using error budgets to balance feature launches against reliability
Aligning product managers, developers and SREs on reliability trade-offs
summary.what_it_does: The page is the listing for a talk at USENIX SREcon16 titled "Service Levels and Error Budgets." The abstract argues that 100% is rarely the right reliability target and that SLAs are not the right tool for SREs to manage a service. It describes setting service level objectives (SLOs) and managing a service to maximize feature velocity within an agreed error budget. The talk covers the differences between indicators, objectives and agreements, error budgets in practice, and how they bring product, development and SRE teams together. The page also lists speaker bios and citation information.
notable: Presented by Google SREs; speaker Chris Jones works on Google App Engine
Covers the SLI, SLO and SLA distinction and error budgets
Co-author Niall Murphy wrote the O'Reilly book Site Reliability Engineering
caveats: The page is a conference talk listing, not a tool; it contains no downloadable material or slides in the text
SREcon16 is sold out and walkup registration is not accepted
